title: A new growth hotspot, an emerging-market darling, and potential trouble in the north
gist: Promotional page for Oxford Economics Africa's Watchlist 2027 webinar (26 Nov 2026), previewing calls that African growth is shifting west on reform momentum while politics weighs on the east, that South Africa could be 2027's emerging-market darling and Namibia its dark horse, and flagging DRC constitutional-change and Morocco-Algeria conflict risks. Only headline views are given, with no supporting data.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics Africa argues the epicentre of African economic growth is shifting westwards, as reform momentum boosts growth in West Africa while political developments could weigh on East Africa heading into 2027.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Suggests rotating African frontier/EM exposure toward reforming West African economies and away from politically exposed East African ones for 2027.
insights.quote: The epicentre of African economic growth is shifting westwards, with reform momentum boosting growth in the west, while political developments could weigh on the east.
insights.locator: The epicentre of African economic growth

themes.theme: South Africa and Namibia 2027 upside calls

insights.claim: Oxford Economics Africa sees South Africa as a candidate to become 2027's emerging-market darling, a view it examines in its Watchlist 2027 outlook.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Flags potential 2027 EM outperformance and inflows into South African assets (rand, SAGBs, equities) worth watching.
insights.quote: examining South Africa’s prospects of becoming 2027’s emerging market darling

insights.claim: Oxford Economics Africa makes the case that Namibia will be Africa's economic dark horse in 2027, i.e. an under-the-radar outperformer.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Namibia is a less-followed frontier market the house expects to surprise to the upside in 2027; worth monitoring for growth and sovereign-credit opportunities.
insights.quote: We also make our case for why we think Namibia will be next year’s economic dark horse.

themes.theme: African political risk: DRC and Morocco-Algeria

insights.claim: Oxford Economics Africa flags a risk of potentially destabilising constitutional changes in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) as a key 2027 political risk.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: DRC instability matters for critical-mineral supply (cobalt, copper) and for miners with DRC exposure; watch constitutional reform moves.
insights.quote: the risk of potentially destabilising constitutional changes in the DRC

insights.claim: Oxford Economics Africa sees an increased possibility of conflict between Morocco and Algeria heading into 2027.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: A North African flare-up would be a tail risk for Algerian gas supply to Europe and for Moroccan assets; a 'trouble in the north' scenario to monitor.
insights.quote: the increased possibility of conflict between Morocco and Algeria
